name: Spawn on a remote host
note: The client asks for an agent; the controller picks the host that holds its home.

steps.label: POST /cli/sessions/v2/spawn
steps.say: The same route the client uses today. It doesn't know or care where the agent will run.

steps.label: placement.choose(agent)
steps.say: Placement picks the host that holds the agent's home. A laptop-pinned agent only ever goes to that laptop.

steps.label: Spawn{agent, harness, resume_id, epoch}
steps.say: Sent over the WebSocket the host opened when it enrolled. The envelope is signed and sequenced, like k2-node compute frames today. The epoch enforces invariant I1.

steps.label: open_session(cols, rows)
steps.say: The host asks its local PTY host for a terminal. The PTY host owns the output ring, so output survives the host link dropping.

steps.label: exec claude --resume <id>
steps.say: The CLI starts exactly as it does today, with K2_CELL, K2_HOOK_SOCK and K2_HOOK_TOKEN set.

steps.label: hook SessionStart (cell socket)
steps.say: Hooks reach the host's per-cell socket. The /proc ancestry owner check runs here, on the same kernel as the CLI.

steps.label: AgentEvent{SessionStart, attested}
steps.say: The controller only accepts events the host has already attributed to the right agent.

steps.label: activity + PTY stream
steps.say: The client sees the agent start and can attach to its terminal through the controller.
